options: This strategy will not solve the problem correctly.

questions.text: Mandatory : No Calculator : None Response Time : N.A Think Time : N.A Minimum Instruction Time : 0 Which of the following statements is true about Dijkstra's algorithm to find the shortest path?
options: Dijkstra’s algorithm may fail for graphs with negative weights because it does not reconsider a node once it marks it as visited, even if a shorter path exists than the previous one.
The shortest path between two vertices u and v in a graph G always remains unaltered when all the edges of G are incremented by an equal amount.
The shortest path between two vertices u and v in a graph G always remains unaltered when all the edges of G are multiplied by a positive integer.
To decide which node to visit next, Dijkstra's algorithm selects the node with the smallest known distance.
correct_answer: Dijkstra’s algorithm may fail for graphs with negative weights because it does not reconsider a node once it marks it as visited, even if a shorter path exists than the previous one.
The shortest path between two vertices u and v in a graph G always remains unaltered when all the edges of G are multiplied by a positive integer.
